official.deadline_note: Deadline is 5 p.m. JST from the host institution to JSPS. Host institutions set their own internal deadlines, which may fall more than one month before the JSPS deadline. The FY2027 1st round (25 September 2026) has closed; the 3rd round closes 4 June 2027.
official.application_cycle: FY2027, open-call rounds: 1st closed 25 September 2026, 2nd deadline 8 January 2027, 3rd deadline 4 June 2027
official.status_note: The FY2027 2nd recruitment is the next live round: applications due 8 January 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results in mid-May 2027, arrival in Japan between 1 August 2027 and 31 March 2028; 20 fellowships are awarded per round. From FY2024, award letters for successful candidates are sent to host institutions.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition support is published; the terms of financial support list a maintenance allowance, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance only.
benefits: Maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month for PhD holders
Maintenance allowance of JPY 200,000 per month for candidates who do not hold a PhD when research starts in Japan
Round-trip air ticket based on JSPS's regulations
Settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 (only for fellowships of three or more months)
Research support allowance for cooperative research expenses, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of the US, Canada, an EU member state, the UK, Switzerland, Norway or Russia, or have been engaged in research continuously for at least three years at a university or research institution in one of those countries (maternity and parental leave months are deducted from the count)

Hold a doctoral degree from a foreign graduate school awarded within six years as of 1 April of the fellowship fiscal year (i.e. on or after 2 April six years prior), or be currently enrolled in a doctoral course at a foreign graduate school and expected to receive the PhD within two years of the fellowship start
Be from a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan, or from Taiwan or Palestine, and possess an excellent research record; employment status is not considered

Not have previously started a fellowship under any JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship (Standard (P), Short-term (PE), Short-term (PA) or Pathway to University positions in Japan (PU)); not hold a resident card with a mailing address in Japan at the application deadline; not be a Japanese citizen who is also a permanent resident of an eligible country
Be hosted by a full-time researcher affiliated with a KAKENHI-eligible institution who submits the application; each host researcher may submit up to three applications
requirements: Applications are submitted by the Japanese host researcher through the JSPS Electronic Application System via the head of the host institution and must reach JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on the round deadline
The host institution's internal deadline applies and may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline
Fellowship tenure must be between 1 and 12 months, with arrival inside the round's published window

A selected fellow must submit the original doctoral degree certificate or diploma (or the prospect certificate if the degree is not yet obtained) before the fellowship start date; submitting it at least three weeks before the start secures the JPY 362,000 monthly rate
The application is completed in Japanese or English; documents in other languages require a Japanese or English translation
documents: FORM1 - application form entered on the JSPS Electronic Application System by the host researcher
FORM2 - application form completed by the foreign candidate
Letter of Recommendation (one page) completed by the candidate's recommender, written in English or Japanese
Doctoral degree certificate or diploma (original copy required after selection, before the fellowship start date)
Prospect certificate for the doctoral degree for candidates who have not yet obtained the degree
selection_criteria: Document review by three examiners on a 1-5 scale (5 superlative to 1 poor), weighing research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged score is the primary screening criterion for the panel review
That the host and candidate have established close communication and devised a concrete research plan
That the host institution has adequately prepared a system for receiving the candidate
That the fellowship contributes to promoting exchange between Japan and the countries of North America and Europe
That preference is not given to host institution or field of specialization in making selections
coverage: Maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month for PhD holders (JPY 200,000 per month for non-PhD holders at the time research starts in Japan)
Round-trip air ticket based on JSPS's regulations
Settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 for fellowships of three months or more
Research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
application_method: Open Call: the head of a Japanese university or research institution applies; the host researcher enters the application in the JSPS Electronic Application System and the institution transmits it to the president of JSPS
A parallel Nomination channel exists through JSPS overseas nominating authorities, separate from the open call
official.application_route: The candidate cannot apply directly - a Japanese host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution submits the application through their institution head via the JSPS Electronic Application System by 5 p.m. JST on the round deadline
official.study_mode: Full-time research fellowship under JSPS's full-commitment requirement
official.citizenship_residency: Citizen or permanent resident of the US, Canada, an EU member state, the UK, Switzerland, Norway or Russia, or researcher with three or more years' continuous research at an institution in one of those countries; those holding a resident card with a Japanese mailing address at the deadline are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Open to overseas researchers only; candidates must be recruited from outside Japan and hosted by a Japanese institution
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences; no field restriction
official.research_requirement: A concrete research plan devised jointly with the host researcher; the document review assesses research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential
official.description: JSPS states the program provides PhD students or PhD researchers in Europe and North America with opportunities to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of their hosts in universities and other Japanese institutions for a relatively short period of time, and that a person who has never engaged in research at universities etc. in Japan would be most preferable. Selection runs through two channels: Open Calls and Nominations.
official.program_type: Postdoctoral research fellowship - Short-term (PE), Open Call
official.english_requirement: No formal English test score is published. The application should be completed in either Japanese or English (proper names and technical terms may be supplemented in either language), and documents not in Japanese or English must be accompanied by a Japanese or English translation

not_confirmed: Formal English-language test score (none published - only the Japanese/English application language rule)
Tax treatment of the maintenance allowance (not addressed on the official pages)
verification.notes: Award amounts, FY2027 round deadlines, forms, selection policy and the JPY 362,000/200,000 PhD-dependent allowance rule were taken directly from JSPS's own Short-term (PE) pages and the December 2025 fellows FAQ; the FY2027 1st round closed on 25 September 2026, so the 2nd round (8 January 2027) is the next open deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a host-driven award: you cannot apply yourself - a Japanese researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution submits the application through their university, so securing the right host is the real competition. With the FY2027 1st round closed on 25 September 2026, the realistic targets are the 2nd round (host institution must transmit by 5 p.m. JST on 8 January 2027) or the 3rd round (4 June 2027). Only 20 fellowships exist per round and FY2026's 2nd round selected 20 of 136 applications (14.7%), so a concrete, well-communicated host-candidate research plan matters more than raw publication count.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers who hold, or are finishing, a PhD from a foreign university inside the six-year window, are citizens or permanent residents of the US, Canada, the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway or Russia, have never held a JSPS postdoctoral fellowship, and have no Japanese mailing address.
application_readiness_checklist: Map the six-year window against 1 April 2027: the doctorate must have been awarded on or after 2 April 2021, or you are enrolled in a doctoral course abroad and expect the PhD within two years of the start
Secure a host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution and agree a concrete 1-12 month research plan with them before they enter FORM1
Ask the host institution for its internal deadline now - JSPS warns it can fall more than one month before the JSPS deadline
Prepare FORM2 and a one-page letter of recommendation (English or Japanese), and agree with your host which review section to use from the FY2027 Review Section Table
If awarded, deliver the PhD certificate to JSPS at least three weeks before the start date - that is what secures the JPY 362,000 monthly rate instead of JPY 200,000
common_rejection_risks: Holding a resident card with a mailing address in Japan at the application deadline - an outright bar
Having previously started any JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship (Standard (P), Short-term (PE) or (PA), or Pathway to University positions (PU))
A research plan that reads as generic, with weak evidence of established host-candidate communication - reviewers score the plan and communication explicitly
Missing the host institution's internal cut-off, which is often the effective deadline
Being a Japanese citizen who also holds permanent residency in an eligible country
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa and residence-permit fees, transport between your home institution and the departure airport, family expenses (the overseas travel insurance does not cover dependants), and any living costs beyond the monthly maintenance allowance
document_audit: Names must be entered in Latin characters in the electronic system (no kanji outside JIS levels, external characters or special fonts) - the entered name appears on the award letter
Any document not in Japanese or English needs a Japanese or English translation attached
The doctoral degree certificate is not required at application, but the original copy must reach JSPS before the fellowship start date
Request the round-specific arrival window from your host early - arrival dates are fixed by round and can push the tenure into the next fiscal year
alerts: FY2027 round deadlines (host institution to JSPS, 5 p.m. JST): 25 September 2026 (closed), 8 January 2027 and 4 June 2027
Results land roughly four months after each deadline (mid-May 2027 for the 2nd round), so plan around the published arrival window, not your own calendar
If you already live in Japan with a mailing address, JSPS will not pay the outbound airfare or the JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance
The research support allowance is applied for by the host researcher through their institution, not by you - agree its use with your host in advance
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The host researcher enters FORM1 in the JSPS Electronic Application System, the institution head approves and the institution transmits to the president of JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on the deadline day; three examiners score the file 1-5 and a panel review selects up to 20 fellows per round

official.deadline_note: Deadline is 5 p.m. JST from the host institution to JSPS; host institutions set internal deadlines that may fall more than one month earlier. The FY2027 1st recruitment deadline was 28 August 2026.
official.status_note: The FY2027 2nd recruitment (Short-term) closes 23 April 2027 at 5 p.m. JST; the JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available about two months before the deadline. Selection results are published in early August 2027, with arrival in Japan between 1 October 2027 and 31 March 2028. The FY2027 1st recruitment (28 August 2026) has closed.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition support is published; the terms of financial support list a round-trip economy air ticket, a JPY 18,000 per-day maintenance allowance, overseas travel insurance and a research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000 only.
benefits: Round-trip air ticket (economy-class), based on JSPS's regulations
Maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day (Short-term)
Research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
An opportunity to conduct collaborative research, discussions and opinion exchanges with researchers in Japan, including lectures and exchange activities
eligibility: Candidate: be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner); persons of Japanese nationality are eligible only if they resided abroad for 10 years or longer at the time of application and are judged by the host institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community

Candidate: be a full-time researcher, or a person with full-time researcher status, at a university or research institution in a foreign country and hold a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor (including positions such as professor emeritus)

Candidate of other status: eligible if it has been six years or longer since obtaining the doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution
Both candidate conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection and during the fellowship period

Applicant (host researcher): be a full-time researcher affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the KAKENHI procedure, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant and wish to host an overseas researcher; host and candidate must have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution through the JSPS Electronic Application System
The host institution's application must reach the president of JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027 for the FY2027 2nd recruitment
The host researcher must choose the review section from the FY2027 Review Section Table, referring to the FY2027 Review Section Set
Before transmitting, the institution must verify institutional approval and check the 'List of Applications' on the electronic system to confirm the registered information is correct

Fellowship tenure is 14 to 60 days; the fellowship period runs from the day the fellow arrives at an airport in Japan to the day the fellow departs from an airport in Japan (this does not apply to fellows residing in Japan before or after the period)
documents: L-1/S-1: items entered on the website - entered by the applicant (host researcher)
S-2: Research Proposal Document - entered jointly by the host researcher and the candidate
S-3: Fellow's Curriculum Vitae - entered by the candidate
FY2027 Review Section Table and FY2027 Review Section Set (PDFs) for selecting the screening section
FY2027 Application Guideline and Instructions for the Application Forms (PDFs)
selection_criteria: Document review by three examiners on a 1-5 scale (5 superlative to 1 poor), weighing research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged score is the primary screening criterion for the panel review
That the collaboration can be expected to advance research in the subject field and to contribute to advancing science in Japan and other countries
That the host researcher and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan

That the plan's objective is lectures, discussions or other exchange activities held not only at the host institution but also at other institutions, including instructive opportunities to foster young researchers

That unbalance is avoided in selectees' nationalities, host institutions and areas of specialization, and that selectees of Japanese nationality number no more than about 3% of all selectees under one recruitment
coverage: Round-trip air ticket (economy-class), based on JSPS's regulations
Maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day (Short-term)
Research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
application_method: Agree a concrete activity plan with the prospective host researcher in Japan; JSPS requires that contact was established in advance
The host researcher enters L-1/S-1 on the JSPS Electronic Application System and obtains approval from the head of the institution
The candidate completes S-3; the host researcher and candidate complete S-2 jointly
The institution transmits the application to the president of JSPS by the deadline (5 p.m. JST, 23 April 2027 for the FY2027 2nd recruitment)
official.application_route: Applied for entirely by the Japanese host researcher, via the head of their institution through the JSPS Electronic Application System; the candidate supplies the S-3 CV and co-writes the S-2 research proposal
official.study_mode: Full-time short-term visit of 14 to 60 days; fellowship days run from arrival at an airport in Japan to departure from an airport in Japan
official.citizenship_residency: Citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwan and Palestine treated in this manner); persons of Japanese nationality only after 10 or more years' residence abroad with host-institution endorsement
official.international_eligibility: Open to overseas researchers only - the candidate must be a full-time researcher at a foreign institution; the Japanese host researcher is the applicant, not the candidate
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences
official.research_requirement: A Research Proposal Document (S-2) completed jointly by the host researcher and the candidate, covering lectures, discussions or other exchange activities
official.description: JSPS states the programs provide excellent researchers from other countries an opportunity to conduct collaborative research, discussions, and opinion exchanges with researchers in Japan, intended to help advance the overseas researchers' research activities while advancing science and promoting internationalization in Japan. The Short-term option invites mid-career and senior researchers for visits of 14 to 60 days for discussions, opinion exchanges and lectures.
official.english_requirement: No formal English test score is published. Forms L-2 and S-2 may be completed in either Japanese or English except in sections where a specific language is required, and the application should otherwise be completed in Japanese or English

not_confirmed: Tuition coverage (no tuition support is published for this fellowship)
Formal English-language test score (none published; L-2/S-2 may be completed in Japanese or English)
verification.notes: The JPY 18,000 per-day allowance, the 14-60 day duration, the FY2027 2nd recruitment deadline of 23 April 2027, the application forms and the selection policy were taken directly from JSPS's own Invitational Fellowships pages and the December 2025 fellows FAQ; FY2026 short-term 2nd recruitment selected 75 of 587 applications (12.8%).

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for this yourself: a Japanese host researcher must nominate you through their institution head via the JSPS Electronic Application System, which opens about two months before the 23 April 2027 deadline for the FY2027 2nd short-term recruitment. The money is a per-diem rather than a salary - JPY 18,000 for every day from your arrival at a Japanese airport to your departure, plus an economy round-trip ticket and insurance - so the visit has to be scoped to fit that daily budget. FY2026's 2nd recruitment was the tighter of the two rounds, at 587 applications for 75 selections (12.8%), and results only appear in early August 2027, so an October 2027 start means committing your calendar months in advance.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career and senior overseas researchers holding a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor (or six-plus years past a doctorate with continuous research abroad) who already have an agreed collaboration plan with a Japanese host and can spend 14-60 days in Japan between October 2027 and March 2028.
application_readiness_checklist: Lock in a Japanese host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution and agree the concrete activity plan - lectures, discussions, exchange - before any form is started, because selection policy explicitly tests that contact was established in advance
Draft S-2 jointly with the host and write S-3 (your CV) yourself; both may be completed in English
Have the host select the right review section from the FY2027 Review Section Table, cross-checking the paired reviewers in the FY2027 Review Section Set
Confirm the host institution's internal deadline, which can be more than one month before 23 April 2027
Scope the visit so the entire 14-60 days fall inside the 1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028 arrival window
common_rejection_risks: No documented prior contact with the host, leaving the S-2 plan reading as theoretical
A plan built around the host institution alone - the policy expects lectures, discussions or exchange activities at other institutions as well, plus instructive opportunities for younger researchers
Candidate status mismatch: neither a professor-equivalent position nor six years past the doctorate
The host institution's internal deadline passing while the team waits on the S-2 joint draft
Relying on the Japanese-nationality route, which is capped at about 3% of selectees per recruitment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the daily allowance: domestic travel outside the airport-to-host route, conference or event fees, accommodation above what JPY 18,000 per day covers in Tokyo or Osaka, and any family travel or insurance (dependants are not covered by the fellowship insurance)
document_audit: S-2 is a joint document - a draft that never gets the host researcher's input will stall in the final weeks
L-1/S-1 website entries are the host researcher's responsibility; you cannot correct them yourself once submitted
If you lecture during the visit, any honorarium must be paid as an honorarium and not as salary, so it does not create an employment relationship
Insured cards are generally not issued for stays of three months or less, so keep the award letter's insurance documentation for visa purposes
alerts: The FY2027 1st recruitment (28 August 2026) has closed; the 2nd short-term deadline is 23 April 2027 at 5 p.m. JST
The fellowship clock runs from landing at a Japanese airport to departing from one - build the budget around actual days in Japan, not calendar weeks
If you hold a mailing address in Japan before the start date, the outbound airfare and the settling-in allowance will not be paid
The research support allowance (up to JPY 150,000) is applied for by the host institution, not by you - agree its intended use in the S-2 plan
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The host researcher enters L-1/S-1 online and prepares S-2 with you, the institution head approves and transmits to the president of JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027; three examiners score the file 1-5 and a panel review then selects about 75 fellows
